Thank you all for those reports. Let me work through this before I make my decision.

First, on the collateral requirement: we have $6,000,000 outstanding, so we need collateral valued at least $7,500,000 after haircuts (1.25 × $6,000,000). The corporate-bond basket Elias identified has a market value of $9,400,000 with a 20% haircut, so the collateral value would be $7,520,000 — that clears the $7,500,000 threshold, but only by $20,000. That's extremely tight. Elias, can you confirm whether the basket has any additional margin or if there's any flexibility there?

Second, Nadia's legal requirements are clear: no more than 30% exposure to any single issuer, and a signed collateral-amendment acknowledgment must be executed before settlement. I'll need confirmation that the basket meets the single-issuer limit and that the acknowledgment is ready to sign.

Third, Victor's custody requirement means this must settle through a segregated custody account within 2 business days. We need to make sure that timeline works.

Finally, Leila's client settlement requires exactly $9,000,000 of government bonds released on 2026-08-19. We currently have $10,000,000 of government bonds pledged, so releasing $9,000,000 would leave only $1,000,000 in government bonds. Combined with the $7,520,000 collateral value from the corporate bonds, total post-haircut collateral would be $8,520,000 — well above the $7,500,000 requirement.

Before I sign off, I need to confirm: (1) the corporate basket meets the 30% single-issuer limit, (2) the collateral-amendment acknowledgment is ready for execution, and (3) the segregated custody settlement can complete within 2 business days aligned with the 2026-08-19 release date. Can each of you confirm your respective items?

Thank you all. Leila's right — we need to make a decision now, and I'm going to make it.

On the cushion question: I've weighed the $20,000 surplus against the timeline risk, and I am not comfortable approving a substitution with only $20,000 of headroom. If market values move even fractionally against us before settlement completes, we fall below the $7,500,000 requirement and we're in breach of the facility — that's an unacceptable risk. However, Elias has flagged that identifying additional collateral adds time, and Nadia has confirmed that any basket change resets her amendment drafting cycle, which compresses the window toward Victor's August 17 initiation deadline.

So here's my decision and my directive to each of you:

First, Elias — I need the issuer-concentration confirmation from your existing analysis as your absolute top priority. That is the fastest path to unblocking Nadia and Victor. In parallel, continue assessing additional collateral, but treat the current basket as the primary path unless you can identify additional qualifying collateral within the next 24 hours. If you can find even a modest amount of supplementary collateral to widen the cushion without resetting the timeline materially, report it. If not, I will make a final call on whether the $20,000 cushion is acceptable given the client settlement imperative.

Second, Nadia — proceed with drafting the amendment acknowledgment template now using the current basket composition as the working draft. If Elias confirms the issuer concentration is within the 30% limit on the current basket, we execute on that draft. If additional collateral is identified and changes the basket, you'll update — but only if that happens within 24 hours. After that, we lock the basket.

Third, Victor — August 17 is our hard initiation deadline. I need you to confirm that the segregated custody account is set up and ready so that the moment you're cleared, there are zero operational delays on your end.

Fourth, Leila — update the collateral release queue immediately after this call, as you said. Confirm back to me when it's done.

I want all four confirmations — issuer concentration, amendment readiness, custody account readiness, and queue update — within 24 hours. At that point I will either sign off on the substitution with the current basket if the cushion is the only remaining issue and the client settlement timeline is at risk, or approve an updated basket if additional collateral has been identified. We are not going to let this drift.
